summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, interstitial lung disease, chronic heart failure, and prior venous thromboembolism was admitted with a one-week history of productive cough, low-grade fever, and worsening proximal muscle pain and weakness. She had been unable to receive her usual rituximab infusion due to insurance delays. Evaluation showed elevated CPK consistent with a mild polymyositis flare, but no need for medication changes. Chest imaging and clinical course supported viral bronchitis without pneumonia. Her warfarin dose was adjusted for a subtherapeutic INR, and she was transitioned to daily 7.5 mg. Due to profound weakness and inability to ambulate safely, she was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation for physical therapy and care coordination. She improved symptomatically during the stay with nebulized treatments and continued home medications.
